To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total cross section of π ∓ -proton scattering has been measured between 70 and 290 MeV and that the absolute accuracy is about 0.5 % for most data points.
the total cross sections for pion-protons between 70 and 290 Mev have been measured with a relative accuracy of 0.5% and an absolute accuracy of 1%.
the pion-proton total cross section measurements are in agreement with previous measurements and are in good agreement with the predictions of the Chew-Low model of strong interactions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the total cross-section data are consistent with the predictions of the Δ 1 0, Δ 1 + resonance model and that no evidence has been found for any additional resonant structure.

, within the limits imposed by the accuracy of the data and the limitations of the theoretical models used, the results are consistent with a simple one-pion exchange picture for the π ∓ N scattering.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Δ 0 resonance is not as strong as previously thought.
the Δ ++ resonance is not a simple Breit-Wigner shape, but is more accurately described by a complex shape with a width of about 30 mev.

, in the region of 70-290 MeV, the total cross-section data for the two charge states of pion are in good agreement with each other and with the predictions of a simple phase-shift model, but that they are not in agreement with the predictions of any of the existing phase-shift analysis programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the total cross sections for pion-protons scattering is very sensitive to the presence of resonances.
the pion-nucleon total cross sections are well described by a simple resonance model.
the total cross sections for pion-protons are much larger than the total cross sections of protons.
